---
title: "Estimator interoperability"
subtitle: "Wide arrays for crabbymetrics and long panels for PyFixest"
---

`pypanelsim` does not impose an estimator interface. A panel exposes wide NumPy
arrays, long columns, observed unit covariates, treatment timing, and causal
truth for evaluation.

```{python}
import crabbymetrics as cm
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pyfixest as pf
import pypanelsim as pps

panel = pps.classic_factor(overlap=0.0, seed=91)
```

## crabbymetrics

crabbymetrics panel estimators consume the wide `(unit, period)` arrays directly.

```{python}
model = cm.AugmentedBalancing(balance="double")
model.fit(panel.outcome, panel.treatment)
balancing_att = float(model.summary()["att"])
pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "quantity": ["estimated ATT", "true ATT", "error"],
        "value": [balancing_att, panel.true_att, balancing_att - panel.true_att],
    }
)
```

An outcome model can be supplied as a same-shaped nuisance surface. The oracle
surface below is for interface demonstration only; a real estimator must fit its
nuisance model without treated post-treatment leakage.

```{python}
oracle = cm.AugmentedBalancing(balance="none")
oracle.fit(panel.outcome, panel.treatment, panel.untreated_outcome)
print(float(oracle.summary()["att"]), panel.true_att)
```

## PyFixest

PyFixest consumes a long DataFrame and formula. `as_long_dict()` supplies all
core panel columns and repeats observed unit covariates over time.

```{python}
long = pd.DataFrame(dict(panel.as_long_dict()))
twfe = pf.feols(
    "outcome ~ treatment | unit + time",
    data=long,
    vcov={"CRV1": "unit"},
)
pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "estimate": [float(twfe.coef()["treatment"])],
        "standard error": [float(twfe.se()["treatment"])],
        "simulation ATT": [panel.true_att],
    }
)
```

The regression coefficient and `panel.true_att` need not target the same
weighted estimand under heterogeneous effects or staggered adoption. The point
of the interchange is to make this comparison explicit, not to force agreement.

## Writable inputs

The package returns read-only arrays by default. Ask for copies when an estimator
modifies its inputs:

```{python}
y_copy, w_copy = panel.as_arrays(copy=True)
print(y_copy.flags.writeable, w_copy.flags.writeable)
```

For selected truth matrices:

```{python}
y0, tau = panel.arrays(("untreated_outcome", "treatment_effect"))
np.testing.assert_allclose(panel.outcome, y0 + tau)
```
